digest.component_or_area: Reconcile Bridge git push and merge recovery
propositions: Bridge delivery is abandoned after a single transient transport fault (TLS handshake, DNS resolution, timeout, promisor fetch failure) because push.py treats all non-fast-forward errors identically and retries only genuine non-fast-forward conflicts, leaving policy declines and transport faults in the same terminal branch.

The push loop has zero backoff and no retry budget for transport-class failures, causing unpushed commits to be silently lost when a converged reconciliation pass encounters a flaky network condition on the runner.

Transport-retriable signatures (certificate verification failed, could-not-resolve-host, connection reset, git timeout 30s, promisor remote fetch failure) must be classified separately from permanent policy violations using a subtractive classifier, with bounded retry (3 attempts) and backoff (0.5s, 2.0s).

Both the explicit fetch in recovery and the on-demand promisor fetch inside git merge must apply the same transport-retriable classifier, because partial-clone `blob:none` fetch operations can fail transiently during conflict resolution.
Policy-decline failures (pre-receive hook, GH013) must remain strictly terminal with zero retries, preserving the existing contract that permanent rule violations do not benefit from replay.
Moving push-failure classification, backoff, and strict-reporting logic to a new module `push_classify.py` is required to keep `push.py` under the 800-LOC hard cap.
